1. Present appeal is filed by the appellant under Section 378 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short "Cr.P.C.") against the judgment and order of acquittal dated 17.1.2023 passed by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No.8, Ahmedabad (hereinafter referred to as "the trial court") in Criminal Case No.2448 of 2007, whereby, the trial Court has acquitted the original NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined accused - Girish Bhogilal Vohra vs Hareshbhai Medharam Waghvani on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471337/

2. It is the case of the appellant that the on 31/07/2006 at 02.00 p.m., the appellant - Food Inspector accompanied by peon, Jayantilal Solanki visited Jai Mithu Products, 155, Kotarpur,
Nobelnagar, Ahmedabad wherein the respondent No.1 was present and doing the business.
One gentleman passing through the area Dayalbhai Vanjumal Jaswani was called as a Panch Witness and in his presence the appellant has disclosed his identity and inquired about the food articles.
2.1 In presence of the panch, the respondent accused informed that the said food article is Cornflour (BBC Brand) and the price of one kg.
plastic bag is Rs.20/-.
The appellant paid Rs.60/- in cash in presence of panch and purchased three bags of Cornflour (BBC Brand) each of one kilogram.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined 2.2

After following the due procedure under the law and after giving the intimation to the accused person in his presence and in the presence of Panch Witness, the sample was collected and necessary Panchnama is made.
2.3 The sample was sent to the Laboratory for the purpose of public analysis.

The report of the Public Analyst reveals that though the ingredients disclosed in the plastic bag reveals that it contains the permitted synthetic colour, however, the same was not found in the sample and thus, the sample was clearly misbranded.
Therefore, after following the due procedure and after receiving the sanction, the complaint was registered against the accused person.
2.4 The charge is framed against the Accused person, wherein the Accused pleaded as not guilty and proceeded to face the trial.
The prosecution has led oral as well as documentary evidence to bring home the charges.
The further statement of the Accused is recorded under Section 313 of the Code.

At the conclusion of the trial, the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/12/2024 undefined trial Court was acquitted the accused by the impugned judgment and order dated 17.1.2023 passed in Criminal Case No.2448 of 2007.
3. Being aggrieved and feeling dissatisfied with the impugned order passed by the trial Court acquitting the present respondent accused, the appellant has preferred present appeal.

4. Heard Ms.Shaili Kapadia, learned Counsel for the appellant and Ms.Megha Chitalia, learned APP for the respondent State of Gujarat.
5.

Ms. Shaili Kapadia, learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that the trial Court has completely overlooked the evidence led by the appellant and thereby the trial Court committed serious error of law and on facts both.

She has further submitted that the evidence led by the prosecution including the oral as well as the documentary more particularly, the analysis report clearly mentioned that the sample was substandard and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined adulterated and therefore, the case for mis-branding and adulteration was lodged against present respondent accused however, without considering and appreciating the same the trial Court has passed the impugned judgment and order of acquittal in favour of respondent accused, which is erroneous, illegal and unjust.

5.1 Learned Counsel for the Girish Bhogilal Vohra vs Hareshbhai Medharam Waghvani on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471337/

sentences.text: appellant has further contended that the public analyst report established the guilt of the present respondent accused, however the same was not properly appreciated by the trial Court while passing the impugned judgment and order of acquittal.

5.2 Learned Counsel for the appellant has further submitted that the complainant Food Inspector,
through his deposition, has established that he is competent to file the prosecution against the present respondent accused and having a valid authorization and also the sanctioned given by the Deputy Commissioner is in consonance with the settled legal principle, however NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined said fact was not properly considered by the trial Court, in its true and proper spirit.

5.3 Learned Counsel for the appellant has further submitted that so far as the manner and method in which the sample was collected and sent, all the statutory procedure under the Act was followed and the sample was sent for the public analyst however, all these facts were not properly appreciated by the trial Court in its true and proper spirit, while passing the impugned judgment and order of acquittal.

5.4 In view of the above submissions, learned Counsel for the appellant submits that the impugned judgment and order of trial Court is not in consonance with the settled legal principle and the same may be quashed and set aside and present appeal filed against the acquittal of the respondents accused may be allowed.
6. I have perused the material available on record as well as the documents appended thereto.
I have also gone through the record of the Appeal and impugned judgment NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined and order of acquittal passed by the trial Court.
I have also examined the evidence recorded by the trial Court.

7. At this juncture, it is required to be noted herein that though the notice served upon the respondent accused, he has chosen not to remain present before the Court and therefore, in his absence the present appeal is decided.

8. After going through the original record of the trial Court and after going through the deposition of the witnesses as well as relevant documentary evidence, the fact reveals that in the deposition of the original complainant, he has admitted in his cross-examination that no ingredient or value was mentioned on the packing of the sample collected by the complainant.
It is also admitted by the Food Inspector that he has not drawn any panchnama of the place while collecting the sample.
He has also admitted that the sample sent for the public analysis was not found adulterated.

He has also admitted in his cross-examination that on receipt of the report, it was found that the sample sent for analysis was not NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined adulterated and therefore, the case is filed for mis- branding of the sample.
In that view of the matter, the trial Court was justified in passing the impugned judgment and order of acquittal in favour of the respondent accused.

So far as the cornflour is concerned, there was no standard prescribed in the scheduled.

Further, there was no standard fixed for the flour articles namely cornflour and therefore, after considering all the aforesaid facts, the trial Court has rightly passed the impugned judgment and order of acquittal in favour of present respondent accused.

Even Mr.
Jayantibhai Gandaji Solanki P.W.2 at Exh.31, in his cross examination has admitted that he has not completed the formality of sealing and packing as prescribed under the statute and under the rules,
and therefore, trial Court has rightly passed the impugned judgment and order of acquittal in favour of present NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined respondent.

10. Even the findings recorded by the trial Court in paragraph No. 7 onwards are in consonance with the settled legal principle and after appreciating the evidence led by the prosecution and after relying upon the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court, the trial Court has come to a conclusion that the prosecution has failed to established the case against the respondent accused and therefore, the trial Court has rightly passed the impugned and order of acquittal in favour of the respondent accused.

Even the case of substandard or mis-branding was also not proved because, there was no specification provided under the scheduled attached to the Act and therefore, under such circumstances the impugned judgment and order passed by the trial Court is just and proper.

11. At this stage, it is appropriate to take into account the decision in case of Gangadhar Yashvant Ramekar vs. Mukeshbhai B. Shah and others reported in 1999(2) GCD 1292 in paragraph No.12 has held as under:-

12.1 In this regard, it may be noted that the evidence of the complainant, at Ex. 31, if perused,
indicates that he had no personal knowledge about the cleaning of bottles in which the samples were taken.
He did not have any information or knowledge as to who cleaned those bottles and when.
It would, therefore, be a matter of doubt whether the bottles were really cleaned or not.

When the bottles were shown to the Panch witness, it transpires from the evidence that the cork was closed and, therefore, in light of the decision of this High Court in the case of Sudhirchandra B. Joshi v.

sentences.text: In view of the above decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court whereby the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that the complainant had no personal knowledge about the appropriate procedure required under the law.

Likewise, herein present case, P.W.2 at Exh.31, in his cross examination has clearly admitted that he has not completed the formality of sealing and packing of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined sample, as prescribed under the statute and the rule which shows that he had no personal knowledge about appropriate procedure.
Even the original complainant, has admitted in his cross-examination that no ingredient or value was mentioned on the packing of the sample collected by the complainant.
Hence, in present case, initial and basic procedure like packing, sealing which is most relevant factor of the case and foundation of the case is not followed.
13. In view of the above facts, I am of the opinion that the trial Court has not committed any error while passing the impugned judgment and order of acquittal.

14. It is also now well settled that while exercising powers under Section 378 of Cr.P.C., if the trial/Special Court while passing the order has committed any illegality or any perversity or has exceeded the jurisdiction, unless and until such facts come on record, the Court is very slow while dealing with an acquittal appeal.

The Hon'ble Apex Court has in a series of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined judgments enunciated the principles while exercising jurisdiction under Section 378 against acquittal, the power of the Appellate Court is inasmuch as re- appreciate the evidence, view or re-consider the evidence and if the Court finds that there is any illegality or any irregularity in the judgment then in that case only, the Court has power to entertain the appeal and interfere with the order of acquittal.

The scope and principles are enunciated by the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Chandrappa and others Vs. State of Karnataka reported in (2007) 4 SCC 415, more particularly paragraphs 42 and 43, which was subsequently re- affirmed by the Hon'ble Apex Court Rajesh Prasad Vs. State of Bihar and another, reported in [2022]
3 SCC 471, wherein, the Hon'ble Apex Court has enunciated the general principles in case of acquittal, more particularly in paragraph 26 the general principles are set out by the Hon'ble Apex Court based upon various decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

At this stage, it would be relevant to refer to the general principles culled out by this Court in Chandrappa and others vs. State of Karnataka , regarding the power of Girish Bhogilal Vohra vs Hareshbhai Medharam Waghvani on 13 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197471337/

sentences.text:
The principles read thus:
"42. .... (1) An appellate court has full power to review, reappreciate and reconsider the evidence upon which the order of acquittal is founded.

(2) The Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 puts no limitation, restriction or condition on exercise of such power and an appellate court on the evidence before it may reach its own conclusion, both on questions of fact and of law.

(3) Various expressions, such as, "substantial and compelling reasons", "good and sufficient grounds", "very strong circumstances", "distorted conclusions", "glaring mistakes", NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/12/2024 undefined etc. are not intended to curtail extensive powers of an appellate court in an appeal against acquittal.

Such phraseologies are more in the nature of "flourishes of language" to emphasize the reluctance of an appellate court to interfere with acquittal than to curtail the power of the court to review the evidence and to come to its own conclusion.
(4) An appellate court, however, must bear in mind that in case of acquittal, there is double presumption in favour of the accused.

Firstly, the presumption of innocence is available to him under the fundamental principle of criminal jurisprudence that every person shall be presumed to be innocent unless he is proved guilty by a competent court of law.
Secondly, the accused having secured his acquittal, the presumption of his innocence is further reinforced, reaffirmed and strengthened by the trial court.

(5) If two reasonable conclusions are possible on the basis of the evidence on record,
the appellate court should not disturb the finding of acquittal recorded by the trial court.

21. In Rajendra Prasad v. State of Bihar, a three-Judge Bench of this Court pointed out that it would be essential for the High Court, in an appeal against acquittal, to clearly indicate firm and weighty grounds from the record for discarding the reasons of the Trial Court in order to be able to reach a contrary conclusion of guilt of the accused.

entities.text: Rajendra Prasad v. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further observed that, in an appeal against acquittal, it would not be legally sufficient for the High Court to take a contrary view about the credibility of witnesses and it is absolutely imperative that the High Court convincingly finds it well-nigh impossible for the Trial Court to reject their testimony.
This was identified as the quintessence of the jurisprudential aspect of criminal justice.

Viewed in this light, the brusque approach of the High Court in dealing with the appeal, resulting in the conviction of Appellant Nos.
1 and 2, reversing the cogent and well-considered judgment of acquittal by the Trial Court giving them the benefit of doubt

, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/12/2024 undefined cannot be sustained."

sentences.text: The Court has framed general guild lines and principles while exercising the power under Section 378 of the Cr.P.C. against the judgment and order of the acquittal and under the general guild lines issued by the Apex Court, this Court is of the opinion that present appeal does not deserve to be entertained and the same requires to be dismissed.

17. On perusal of the impugned judgment and order, it clearly transpires that the trial Court has not committed any error of fact and law in appreciating the evidence on record and in acquitting the accused from the charges levelled against him.
Even, on reappreciation of the evidence, it clearly transpires that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the charge levelled against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
Therefore, the impugned judgment and order of the trial Court is sustainable and the present appeal is liable to be dismissed.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.A/1027/2013 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/12/2024 undefined 18.
In view of the above, the present appeal is devoid of merits and it deserves to be dismissed.
Resultantly, it is dismissed.
The impugned judgment and order of acquittal passed by the trial Court is hereby confirmed.
Bail bond if any, stands cancelled.
Record and proceedings be sent back to the concerned Trial Court forthwith.
